learningObjective: Distinguish structural and access-pattern properties of NVIDIA GPU memory tiers (register file, shared memory, constant memory, global memory).

canonicalClaims.claim: On sm_80, the per-SM register file (256 KB) is larger than the per-SM configurable L1/SMEM partition (up to 192 KB).
nonImplications: Does not imply that program-visible SMEM per block is 192 KB; the block-level cap is smaller.
Does not imply this ordering holds on other architectures (e.g., Hopper differs).

canonicalClaims.claim: Bank conflicts affect shared memory access when a warp's threads target different addresses within the same bank; global memory has no bank concept, but does have coalescing rules for cross-warp access patterns.
nonImplications: Broadcast (all threads access same address in shared memory) is not a conflict.
A single 128-byte coalesced global-memory transaction is not analogous to a bank conflict.

canonicalClaims.claim: Constant memory is optimized for broadcast: when all threads of a warp read the same address, a single access serves the entire warp.
conditions: Address is uniform across the warp; otherwise accesses serialize.
nonImplications: Non-uniform reads of constant memory can be slower than shared or L1 accesses.
Constant memory has size limits (~ 64 KB), so it is not a substitute for SMEM at scale.

misconceptions.claim: HBM aggregate bandwidth exceeds the aggregate shared-memory bandwidth across all SMs.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Shared memory (SRAM) delivers far higher aggregate per-second bandwidth than HBM; that's why on-chip data reuse is a fundamental optimization.

misconceptions.claim: Global memory has banks and can bank-conflict just like shared memory.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Global memory uses coalescing rules on 32/64/128-byte transactions; it is not bank-partitioned like SMEM.

misconceptions.claim: Constant memory automatically speeds up any read of the same variable across threads; even non-uniform access is broadcast.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The broadcast optimization applies only when all threads read the same address; non-uniform accesses serialize.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: CUDA C++ Programming Guide, constant memory section

misconceptions.claim: Register file per SM is smaller than SMEM per SM on A100; therefore SMEM is preferable for scratchpads.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Register file is 256 KB per SM on A100, larger than the 192 KB L1/SMEM partition; also, registers are per-thread private, so their aggregate capacity is very different from SMEM's block-shared capacity.

implementationFacts: sm_80 register file: 65,536 × 32-bit = 256 KB per SM
sm_80 L1/SMEM: up to 192 KB per SM (configurable), max 163 KB shared per block
sm_80 constant memory: 64 KB total, cached with broadcast optimization
performanceScenarios: Data reuse patterns (blocked GEMM, stencils) exploit SMEM/registers to avoid HBM traffic; kernel design should map data to the appropriate tier.
